case.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
case.limits: Section 230 protects the republication of someone else's content. A generated sentence has no other author to point at, and courts have so far been unwilling to assume the answer.
case.holding: Section 230 bars treating an interactive computer service as the publisher of information provided by another, and notice of the content does not remove that protection.
case.why_ai_cites_it: The foundation of every argument that an AI provider is a conduit for material originating elsewhere. Whether a model output counts as information provided by another information content provider is the unresolved question underneath a growing share of AI defamation claims.

reading.body:
Zeran v. AOL is the case AI providers reach for first when arguing they cannot be held liable as publishers, but whether it actually applies to model-generated output remains an open legal question.

The Fourth Circuit held in 1997 that Section 230 bars treating an interactive computer service as the publisher of content provided by a third party, and that notice of the content does not strip that protection away. The doctrine was built around a clear factual premise: someone else wrote the material, and the platform merely carried it. That premise is straightforward when a user posts a message. It becomes fragile when the output is generated by the service itself, because there is no other author to point at.

Four live cases against Character Technologies are currently testing exactly this boundary. The unresolved question in each is whether a model's output qualifies as information provided by another information content provider under the statute's own terms. Courts have not yet answered that, and the data here does not predict how they will. What it does show is that a single 1997 ruling is now carrying significant doctrinal weight in AI liability disputes, in circumstances its authors did not contemplate.

section.name: AI Case Law: The Precedents Behind the Defenses
